text:
ashley-support: FYI — support ticket 88672: customer reports big p95/p99 latency regressions for text-gen in us-east-1 since last night. They see slow tails (~800-1200ms) while p50 unchanged. :eyes:

 tom-runtime: seeing the same in canary -> p99 jumped ~350ms right after rollout window at 02:10 UTC. No error rate spike, just latency.

 maria-sre: what changed in runtime? kernel, conn pooling, TLS stack? Can we get a flamegraph?

 kevin-deploy: deploy-bot shows rollout of runtime v2.9.4 with config flag `enable_keepalive=false` (forced by new http-client).

 ashley-support: customer includes traces showing increased TLS handshake durations and short-lived connections. They hit our /v1/generate endpoint with many short requests.

 on-formatted snippet from traces (customer):
```
span: tls.handshake
duration: 80-450ms (p95/p99)
span: request.queue.wait  -> small
span: inference  -> normal
```

 maria-sre: that suggests connection churn -> expensive TLS handshakes are dominating tail latency. Can we check TCP/TLS metrics + keepalive counts?

 telemetry-bot: prom query -> `sum(rate(tls_handshake_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(tls_handshake_duration_seconds_count[5m]))` shows average handshake latency up 5x on canary nodes. `tcp_connections_closed_total` also up.

 tom-runtime: confirmed. The only notable change in v2.9.4 is the http-client rewrite that defaulted keepalive to OFF to simplify connection lifetime semantics. Looks like many customers using short-lived sync calls are impacted.

 ashley-support: customer is on hosted API, high volume of short requests from many ephemeral clients (serverless frontends). They saw sudden bill spike too because of tokenization/retries but main complaint is latency.

 maria-sre: mitigation plan options: 1) revert flag in canary to enable keepalive, 2) route traffic for impacted customers away from canary to stable, 3) add an L7 shim to pool connections, 4) recommend customer to enable connection reuse.

 kevin-deploy: I can rollback the flag in canary quickly (hotpatch). If it reduces TLS handshakes p99 back to baseline we can roll to prod revert. Want to validate on a subset first.

 on-blocking repro steps for SRE (quick):
```
# simulate many short requests
for i in $(seq 1 500); do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
# or use wrk for concurrency
wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s --latency https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

 maria-sre: also check TLS session reuse: `ngrep` on canary nodes shows `Connection: close` being sent by our client (so server closes socket after each response). That lines up with enable_keepalive=false.

 omission: deploy-bot: started hotpatch: revert http-client keepalive flag on canary pool (canary-id: canary-42).

 kevin-deploy: hotpatch applied to 3/10 canary nodes. Observability: p99 tail dropping on those nodes already ~120ms improvement.

 ashley-support: customer confirmed improved tail in their tests when routed away from hot canary. :white_check_mark: 

 maria-sre: plan: finish hotpatch rollout across canary, then push a config bump to stable to revert the default (need coordinated changelog + CVE/compat note). Also add integration test that simulates high connection churn.

 tom-runtime: will open PR to set default keepalive=true and add QA test that runs short-request workload. Also adding a feature flag so we can opt-out per-tenant.

 oncritical followups: add telemetry: `tls_handshake_duration_seconds{canary="true"}` tagging and alert when p95 handshake > 200ms and connections_closed rate > baseline * 3.

 ashley-support: I'll update ticket 88672 with mitigation steps and ETA. Customer asked for a postmortem once stabilized.

 onblocking note from oncall-sre: we should consider connection pooling at the edge LB level to protect older clients from short-lived requests if future client changes break keepalive.

 kevin-deploy: rolling out hotpatch to remaining canary nodes now. I'll monitor for regressions.

 maria-sre: after full canary hotpatch we should run a targeted bisect if any residual tails remain: exclude kernel changes first, then network/http-client.

 ashley-support: Thanks team — will post update in support ticket and notify customer. :pray:

 oncall-sre: tagging for follow-up: @tom-runtime @kevin-deploy @maria-sre @ashley-support
